text: About 230 years ago, writers, painters and musicians in Europe began to turn against the strict rules of art.
Earlier, young German writers such as Goethe had already rebelled against rules in the name of passion.
src: from the 1790s prized feeling, imagination and nature over the rules and reason that had governed the arts of the 18th century / Arose in Germany and Britain in the 1790s
young writers rebelled against rules in the name of passion and genius / Johann Wolfgang von Goethe’s The Sorrows of Young Werther of 1774 moved a generation of readers

text: The Romantics believed that feelings and imagination mattered more than fixed rules.
They loved wild nature, like the mountains and seas in the paintings of Caspar David Friedrich.
src: made feeling and imagination central to art / It rejected the faith that universal reason and fixed rules could govern art and life
They sought the sublime in storms, the Alps and the ocean / the solitary figures before mountains and seas in the paintings of Caspar David Friedrich

text: Lord Byron became the most famous poet in Europe.
In a cold summer by Lake Geneva, his ghost-story contest led Mary Shelley to write Frankenstein.
src: Lord Byron’s Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage, from 1812, made its author the most famous poet in Europe
The cold, wet summer of 1816 / kept Lord Byron and his guests indoors at the Villa Diodati by Lake Geneva, where his ghost-story contest led Mary Shelley to write Frankenstein

text: For many Romantics, music, which speaks without words, was the highest art of all.
The Polish pianist Frédéric Chopin turned the memory of his country into music, his mazurkas and polonaises.
src: music, which speaks without words, became for many the highest art of all
the Polish pianist Frédéric Chopin, who settled in Paris in 1831 as the November Uprising in Poland was crushed, turned the memory of his country into mazurkas and polonaises

text: Sympathy for the Greeks, stirred up by Byron, helped bring Britain, France and Russia into their fight for independence.
But love of one's own nation could also turn into hostility towards neighbours and minorities.
src: European sympathy for the Greeks, roused by Byron and the philhellenes, helped bring the intervention of Britain, France and Russia that led to the Battle of Navarino in 1827 and to Greek independence
the love of the national past could turn into hostility towards neighbours and minorities

text: The Brothers Grimm collected fairy tales, and in Finland old songs were gathered into the Kalevala, the epic of Finland.
Today the Grimms' tales are read in many languages, and Chopin's music still fills concert halls.
src: the Brothers Grimm their tales from 1812 / Elias Lönnrot publishes the Kalevala, the epic of Finland, from songs collected in Karelia
The Grimms’ tales are read in scores of languages / the music of Schubert, Chopin and Berlioz fills concert halls
